title: Personnel and charts for the 1967 film band
summary: The band included Clark Terry, Snooky Young, Willie Smith, Nat Pierce and Randy Brecker, with charts by Billy Byers, Bill Holman, Andy Gibson, Billy May, and an Ellington Jeep's Blues.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Oh, Willy Smith, Clarke Terry, Snooky Young, Nat Pierce, Richie Kamuka, Danny Bank, -- let's see --
Jimmy Cleveland, Randy Brecker, Clyde Reisinger, Stevie Little. It was a real strong band.
Clarke Terry, did I mention him?
Eddie Jones on bass. It was the band we played Basin Street East with.

Oh, a whole bunch -- well, let's see, Billy Byers, Bill Holman, and -- well, they did the majority of them. And of course there's a montage there that was really a collection of parts out of different arrangements, you know. Andy Gibson, William Moore, Jr., and Billy May. And then there's -- let's see, there's, "Jeeps Blues," on there, the original Ellington arrangement, with Willy Smith doing it this time. And Clarke Terry does his Mumbles with the big band.
Gee, that would be great to see and hear here.
Well, I'll give you a tape.
Love it. Love it. And what, the man who made it is whom?
Skinner. His name is Skinner. Chuck Skinner.
